Start project by setting your own goals/dates

Can do any number of projects or tasks as long as they meet the following:
- Takes approximately ___ hours in sum total
- Have at least 1 task/project contribute to the course or community
- Have most of the work be a stretching experience that tests and improves existing skills

This project does not necessarily have to be completed. One of the biggest learning moments is failing a project and learning the extent of your abilities. The key deliverables for this project are:
- Some proof of the work that was accomplished and time spent
- Self assessment writing about the experience, what was learned, and what grade they deserve

In the self-assessment
- If project not completed, explain what is done and steps to complete or lessons learned, why stopping, challenges faced, resources used to overcome
- If complete, give a similar justification, ask if it is best work, consider a new stretch, future goal
- Essentially, what did you do, how much time/effort you spent, what went well, what didn’t go well, future goals

Suggestions for course contribution:
- Change outdated information or code in the textbook
- Add additional readings or dictionary items
- Add functionality to course chatbot
- Teach a new tool/subject in class

Suggestions for personal project:
- List the businesses you know someone personally, consider AI use cases that would benefit them
- Pick a charity or cause and design an agent with someone in that community in mind
- Find a use case for the industry you plan to move into
- Ask a professor if there is something they would like made
- Look at what skills you have fallen short on and ask what kind of project would develop that further
- Create an agent that will help with your current job
- Build an agent on a resume website that potential employers can interact with

The student may do multiple projects/tasks as long as it is reasonable and does not far exceed the hours expectation.
